name: PageRank
miniText: How can hyperlink structure define a page's relative importance? NetLogo PageRank compares two agent-based ways to distribute rank over directed links, making mass flow and random-surfer behavior visible. Brin and Page [1] give the search-engine context, Bianchini and colleagues [2] analyze PageRank mathematically, and Kleinberg [3] supplies a related but distinct link-authority approach. Damping changes the balance between following links and redistributing visits, while graph structure controls which nodes collect rank. The model illustrates a ranking measure rather than answering a content query. Direction, dangling nodes, normalization, and the chosen update procedure are essential assumptions. Rank need not measure factual quality, fairness, or relevance to a particular user. Agreement between two numerical procedures can corroborate their shared mathematical target, but it does not empirically validate the assumption that incoming links indicate usefulness.
